source.title: It's Not Just a Phase: On Investigating Phase Transitions in Deep Learning-based Side-channel Analysis
source.authors: Sengim Karayalçin; Marina Krček; S. Picek

record.file_problem: The text is the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Applies mechanistic analysis to side-channel models and reports performance transitions and learned structures on physical trace datasets, a new setting relative to the small algorithmic grokking tasks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own PI and probe trajectories, descriptions of features at training epochs, and activation-patching outcomes. These are included where they bear on the tested versions. Prior-work claims are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The paper borrows the grokking analogy and uses sudden test-PI jumps as a tool to locate features for interpretation. It never shows a delay beyond training fit. Train-vs-test timing is not described in the text. It reports no small algorithmic datasets, no training-set-size sweep, and no init-scale or weight-norm manipulation. It has no progress measures that precede the jump: probe accuracies rise together with PI. None of its results decide whether a grokking version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that mechanistic interpretability of side-channel networks is feasible without mask knowledge, and that studying structures learned during discrete performance jumps is effective. They find evidence of weak universality across targets and reverse-engineer mask values, fully for CHES_CTF/ESHARD and only partially for ASCAD. They frame the jumps as phase transitions analogous to grokking but do not claim to test grokking.
record.recipe_differences: Trains MLPs and a CNN on AES side-channel traces and studies perceived information, probes, PCs, and activation patches; it does not reproduce small modular-arithmetic grokking experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The transition and learned structures differ across datasets: CHES_CTF has two PI increases and an even-odd HW distinction, ESHARD has one increase and no even-odd distinction, ASCAD has staged bit features, and the ASCAD CNN increases more gradually. ASCAD patching requires different components and remains incomplete.

fits_no_version.finding: In side-channel MLPs, interpretable share-leakage features (high-low HW, then even-odd HW; input bits, then output bits) appear at discrete test-performance jumps. The second CHES_CTF jump seems to build on the refined first-stage features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training on masked side-channel data proceeds in discrete feature-acquisition steps, each tied to an interpretable structure, with later steps building on earlier ones.

fits_no_version.finding: Similar high-low HW structures emerge in models trained on different targets and measurement domains (power vs EM). The authors read this as weak universality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Similar structures recur across different side-channel targets. This differs from V6, which concerns repeated runs on the same task.

record.problems: Many trajectory and feature results are described qualitatively from plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The analysis focuses on selected models that already break targets; it does not report repeated-run variability or controlled sweeps over dataset size, initialization, or weight norm. ASCAD patching does not fully recover the expected shares.

untested.parts: All: no algorithmic datasets, no train-saturation-then-test-jump, no dataset-size dependence.
All: no continuous progress measure shown to precede the jump; no memorization removal.
All: whether a delay beyond training fit exists on traces is not shown; no init-scale or weight-norm switch.
All: Adam with L1 regularization only on CHES_CTF/ESHARD; no weight-decay, critical-size or ungrokking tests.
All: no repeated runs on the same task.

missing.what: Training-set PI trajectories, needed to tell whether test jumps lag training fit (a grokking-like delay).
missing.locator: Figure 4 (CHES_CTF), Figure 9 (ESHARD): train and test PI plotted but not described in text

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' with V2/V3 support overstates the link. The paper motivates itself by analogy to grokking work (it cites the originals 2201.02177 and 2301.05217) and uses sudden jumps only to choose epochs for analysis. Its trajectory results are described qualitatively and lack a train-vs-test delay. Its probes rise with, not before, the jumps.

versions.untested_parts: Does not study small algorithmic training sets, perfect training accuracy with chance test accuracy, or how delay changes as training-set size shrinks.

Does not track removal of memorizing components. It studies features and causal effects around performance changes, but does not establish that continuous measures generally anticipate the test-performance jump.
Tests transitions on side-channel physical traces, not the listed image, text, or molecule settings. Does not vary initialization scale or weight norm to switch the effect on or off.
Does not test weight decay as an efficiency bias, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Does not compare repeated runs of the same task to establish convergence to the same algorithm, or test dependence on architecture and hyperparameters.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax explanations of grokking.

rows.subject: CHES_CTF MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured training and test perceived information (PI) during training.
rows.baseline: A plateau in PI before the increase
rows.value: The initial increase starts at epoch 15 and is completed around epoch 40.
rows.note: The text describes an initial performance increase on the test traces; it does not give numeric PI values.
rows.check: Test-PI plateau then rise. The text does not say training PI saturated beforehand, so a grokking-like delay beyond overfitting cannot be read. Not a V2 measure.

source_check.problem: PI timing alone does not establish the delayed generalization or training-regime dependence named in V3.

rows.subject: CHES_CTF MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured training and test perceived information (PI) during training.
rows.baseline: A second plateau in PI before the increase
rows.value: A second increase occurs between epochs 70-85, after which there are no more significant changes in PI.
rows.note: The text describes the timing and plateau, but gives no numeric PI values.
rows.check: Second test-PI rise. Same issue: no stated train-vs-test gap. No V2 link: it is not a progress measure anticipating the jump.

source_check.problem: The second PI increase does not establish V3's delay relative to training fit or training-regime dependence.

rows.subject: CHES_CTF MLP
rows.operation_detail: Examined logits and activation PCs at epochs after the performance increases.
rows.measure: Class separation in logits and first-layer PCs
rows.baseline: Before the first increase, not stated
rows.value: After the first increase, predictions distinguish high from low Hamming-weight values; a diagonal division in the first-layer PCs corresponds to high versus low HWs of the two secret shares.
rows.note: The authors interpret the PC structure as embeddings of the two shares.
rows.check: Feature description after the jump. It does not measure gradual circuit formation before the jump or removal of memorization.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, Figure 3, epoch-50 discussion; Appendix C.

rows.subject: CHES_CTF MLP
rows.operation_detail: Examined logits and activation PCs at epochs after the performance increases.
rows.measure: Class separation in logits and first PCs
rows.baseline: The high-low HW separation seen at epoch 50
rows.value: The model additionally separates even from odd HWs; the PC embedding shows a grid structure, with about nine changes in even-odd corresponding to the nine possible HW values.
rows.note: The paper describes the later feature as a refinement following the earlier high-low separation.
rows.check: Post-jump feature description; not a V2 progress measure.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, Figure 3, epoch-100 discussion; Appendix H.2.

rows.subject: CHES_CTF MLP
rows.operation_detail: Patched a PC to an extreme grid value to fix one share and examined the resulting model outputs and extracted shares.
rows.measure: Whether predictions depend mainly on the unpatched share as expected
rows.value: Fixing a PC to an extreme results in predictions based mainly on the other PC, as expected when one share is fixed; extracted shares are shown with SNR spikes at the corresponding leakage points.
rows.note: This validates causal effects of the learned share-related structure; it does not test removal of memorizing components.
rows.check: Activation patching validates learned share features. Unrelated to grokking timing or mechanism.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, Activation Patching; Figure 5 caption specifies PC0=-20.

rows.subject: ESHARD MLP
rows.baseline: Before epoch 4, test PI had not become positive
rows.value: At epoch 4, perceived information becomes positive and the models start to generalize.
rows.note: The text reports one test-set transition.
rows.check: PI becomes positive at epoch 4, very early. No stated training-fit delay before it.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix E, opening paragraph and Figure 9; Appendix C.
source_check.problem: Positive test PI at epoch 4 does not establish V3's delayed generalization or training-regime dependence.

rows.subject: ESHARD MLP
rows.operation_detail: Examined logits and activation PCs around the transition.
rows.measure: High-low HW distinction in model outputs and PC embeddings
rows.value: The model distinguishes high from low HWs and maps HWs of secret shares onto specific features; the model cannot distinguish even from odd HWs.
rows.note: High-low structure is reported, while the more refined even-odd distinction found for CHES_CTF is absent.
rows.check: Post-transition feature description. The 'partial' state is relative to CHES_CTF, not to any version.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix E, high-low versus even-odd discussion; Figure 10 caption and accompanying text.

rows.subject: ESHARD MLP
rows.operation_detail: Rotated PC coordinates, patched them, and examined extracted share distributions and SNR.
rows.measure: Agreement of patched share distributions with expected secret-share HW distributions
rows.baseline: Actual secret-share distributions shown for comparison
rows.value: The patching results closely match the actual distributions of secret-share HWs.
rows.note: The paper reports the qualitative comparison, without numeric agreement values.
rows.check: Patching result about share extraction; not a grokking measure.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix E.1, comparison of Figure 11 with Figure 10's actual share-HW distributions.

rows.subject: ASCAD MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured PI and linear-probe accuracies for input and output bits during training.
rows.baseline: PI was not positive before the transition; numeric chance accuracy not stated
rows.value: PI transitions to positive between epochs 8-12, corresponding to increased probe accuracies for the input bits.
rows.note: The text reports the timing and association, but not the numeric probe accuracies.
rows.check: Transition at epochs 8-12, with probe accuracies rising at the same time, not beforehand. No train-vs-test gap stated.

source_check.problem: Concurrent PI and probe-accuracy increases do not establish V3's delay relative to training fit or training-regime dependence.

rows.subject: ASCAD MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured PI and linear-probe accuracies for input and output bits during training.

conditions.value: Two least significant S-box output bits

rows.baseline: Other bits only marginally improve over random guessing
rows.value: PI increases marginally until improvement stops at epoch 25; this is accompanied by increasing probe accuracies for the two least significant S-box output bits, which achieve far higher accuracies than the other bits.
rows.note: The later feature progress accompanies marginal PI improvement, not a reported second large PI jump.
rows.check: Marginal later PI gain with output-bit probes. Not a delayed jump and not a V2 anticipating measure.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, Figure 6 discussion of marginal PI improvement through epoch 25 and output-bit probes.

rows.subject: ASCAD MLP
rows.operation_detail: Examined logits and activation PCs for input and output bits.

conditions.value: Two least significant S-box input bits

rows.value: Logits are distributed according to the two input bits; the first two PCs in the second layer show an emerging grid structure corresponding to combinations of mask values.
rows.note: The grid has a 3 × 3 structure rather than the ideal 4 × 4.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, Figure 7 discussion of epoch 12, second-layer PCs and 3×3 versus 4×4 grids.

rows.subject: ASCAD MLP
rows.operation_detail: Examined logits and activation PCs for input and output bits.

conditions.value: Two least significant S-box output bits

rows.baseline: The epoch-12 PCs remain related to input bits
rows.value: Output-bit logits have significantly higher mean values and are spread across fewer values; a visually similar grid appears in the third and fourth PCs for output bits.
rows.note: This describes a later-emerging representation for output bits.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, epoch-25 discussion, footnote 10 and Figure 7 caption.

rows.subject: ASCAD MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained final-layer probes and selectively patched PC components to intervene on share-related features.
rows.measure: Causal effects on probe outputs and recovery of share values
rows.baseline: Expected four classes for the shares
rows.value: Patching has causal effects and yields a reasonable clustering, but SNR values are significantly lower than for actual shares; recovered shares produce only two or three classes where four are expected, and reversed shares do not combine to the correct input-bit label.
rows.note: The authors state that further post-processing is needed to recover actual values.
rows.check: Patching-method quality (incomplete share recovery). This is the study's own method performance, not a claim result.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix F, Figure 12 discussion: lower SNR, two or three recovered classes instead of four, and further processing required.

rows.subject: ASCAD CNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured PI and probe accuracies during training and examined final-model PCs.

conditions.value: Initial smaller jumps followed by a more gradual performance increase

rows.value: The same bits as in the ASCAD MLP show significantly increased accuracies, but the performance increase is more gradual; the authors report that this makes structures harder to find.
rows.note: The text does not provide numeric PI or probe values.
rows.check: CNN performance rises gradually after small jumps. No delayed generalization relative to training fit is described.

source_check.problem: The CNN's performance trajectory does not establish V3's delayed generalization or training-regime dependence.

rows.subject: ASCAD CNN
rows.operation_detail: Examined PC structure in the final model.
rows.measure: Location of share-related structures in the first four PCs
rows.value: Shares are in the first four PCs; input shares correspond to PCs 0 and 2, and output shares to PCs 1 and 3.
rows.note: The authors focus on the final model because performance increases steadily.
rows.check: Final-model PC location of shares; unrelated to grokking.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix G, final paragraph and Figure 14 caption.

relation.reason: The grokking analogy motivates locating and interpreting performance jumps; the experiments concern learned leakage features and mask recovery rather than testing the catalog's grokking claims.

tranche.reason: The study uses performance transitions to identify representations and validate its interpretability and mask-extraction method. It does not establish delayed generalization beyond training fit or directly test another listed claim version.

source_check.notes:
The supplied text is arXiv v3, titled Interpreting Emergent Features in Deep Learning-based Side-channel Analysis; the pack uses a different title. No listed claim version warrants a verdict.
For precision, r12's output-logit analysis conditions on the two input bits being 00; r15's PC structures are measured after the third convolutional block.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: PI increases accompany staged share-related structures, and patching validates causal effects of those structures (r1-r8).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Input-bit and output-bit representations emerge at different training stages, with later PCs encoding output shares in the CNN (r9-r12, r14-r15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Patching has causal effects but share extraction is incomplete: fewer classes than expected and incorrect recombination for input-bit labels (r13).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Side-channel trace datasets CHES_CTF, ESHARD, and ASCAD
reader_labels.reason: The study reports test-PI/generalization increases during training on physical trace datasets (r1, r2, r6, r9, r10, r14).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: These are AES side-channel tasks, and the study does not vary initialization scale or weight norm; it therefore does not establish the broader non-algorithmic-data or regime-switch claims (r1, r2, r6, r9, r10, r14).
